user.title: Add a location to monitor
user.description: Pick the exact spot to watch. An alert only counts if this point is inside the warning polygon, not merely somewhere in the same county. More alert types, notifications and message text can be set under **Configure** after setup.

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach api.weather.gov. Try again in a minute.
error.invalid_location: The NWS API rejected this location. It only covers the United States and its territories.

abort.already_configured: This location is already being monitored.

data.include_zone_alerts: Also match alerts without a polygon

data_description.other_events: Any NWS event name. You can type one that isn't in the list.
data_description.include_zone_alerts: Watches and many advisories cover whole counties or zones and have no polygon. When on, they match if your zone is included. When off, only alerts whose polygon contains your location count.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to ask api.weather.gov for alerts (30–900 seconds).

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Events for automations (`nws_polygon_alerts_new_alert`, `_alert_updated`, `_alert_cleared`) are always fired, whatever you choose here.

data.persistent_notification: Show a notification in Home Assistant
data.notify_on_update: Notify again when an alert is updated

data_description.notify_services: For example notify.mobile_app_your_phone. Leave empty to rely on events or entities only.
data_description.critical_events: For mobile app targets these break through Do Not Disturb and silent mode (iOS critical alert / Android alarm channel).
data_description.notify_on_update: NWS re-issues a warning with a new ID when it's extended or changed. Off means you're only alerted the first time.

messages.title: Message text
messages.description: Titles and messages are Home Assistant templates. You can use `location`, `event`, `headline`, `description`, `instruction`, `area`, `severity`, `certainty`, `urgency`, `sender`, `sent`, `effective`, `expires`, `ends` and `url`, for example `{{ headline }}`. Clear a field to go back to the default.
